<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the universally quantified error data e for the three-level computation.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For natural numbers b and m, a record of four real-valued arrays: p on Fin((b*m)*m), a on Fin(m) × Fin(m) × Fin(b), c on Fin(m) × Fin(m), and d on Fin(m). The constructor imposes no bounds on these arrays.",
      "name": "Error-data record",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the hypothesis e.Valid u; it bounds every supplied perturbation, including entries unused by the algorithm.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For any b,m, error record e=(p,a,c,d), and real u, validity means: |p(k)|≤u for every k∈Fin((b*m)*m); |a(s,j,i)|≤u for every s,j∈Fin(m), i∈Fin(b); |c(s,j)|≤u for every s,j∈Fin(m); and |d(s)|≤u for every s∈Fin(m). All four requirements hold together.",
      "name": "Uniform componentwise error bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "At k=K=b+2*(m−1), supplies the exact coefficient K*u/(1−K*u) multiplying the sum of absolute products.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For real u and natural k, define γ(u,k)=((k cast to the reals)*u)/(1−(k cast to the reals)*u). This definition is total under Lean's real division convention, including division by zero.",
      "name": "Gamma coefficient",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the computed scalar whose absolute difference from the exact dot product is bounded.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For natural b,m, real arrays x,y on Fin((b*m)*m), and e=(p,a,c,d), let B(s,j) be D010 and S be D011. The output is S_m(s ↦ S_m(j ↦ B(s,j), j ↦ c(s,j)), s ↦ d(s)). Thus each block is summed internally, block results are summed within each s, and those results are summed over s.",
      "name": "Three-level perturbed dot product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls the multiplicative perturbation of each addition in the middle summation level.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For any b,m and error record e, projects its third field c: Fin(m) → Fin(m) → ℝ, indexed by s,j.",
      "name": "Middle-level addition errors",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls the multiplicative perturbation of each addition within a block.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For any b,m and error record e, projects its second field a: Fin(m) → Fin(m) → Fin(b) → ℝ, indexed by s,j,i.",
      "name": "Within-block addition errors",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Shows that error records can be formed from arbitrary arrays; the magnitude restrictions are separate hypotheses.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any natural b,m, constructs an error record from p:Fin((b*m)*m)→ℝ, a:Fin(m)→Fin(m)→Fin(b)→ℝ, c:Fin(m)→Fin(m)→ℝ, and d:Fin(m)→ℝ, in that order.",
      "name": "Error-record constructor",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Each exact product x(k)y(k) is multiplied by 1+p(k).",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For any b,m and error record e, projects its first field p:Fin((b*m)*m)→ℝ.",
      "name": "Product errors",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls the multiplicative perturbation of additions at the outermost summation level.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For any b,m and error record e, projects its fourth field d:Fin(m)→ℝ.",
      "name": "Outermost addition errors",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines each length-b block result fed into the two length-m summations.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For natural b,m, arrays x,y on Fin((b*m)*m), error record e, and s,j∈Fin(m), define B(s,j)=S_b(i ↦ (x(ι(s,j,i))*y(ι(s,j,i)))*(1+p(ι(s,j,i))), i ↦ a(s,j,i)), using the sequential sum S of D011 and indexing map ι of D012.",
      "name": "Perturbed block dot product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the exact summation algorithm and order at all three levels. A length-n nonempty sum has n−1 perturbed additions; the first error entry is unused.",

      "meaning": "For natural n and real arrays t,δ on Fin(n), S_n(t,δ)=0 if n=0. If n>0, start A_0=t(0); for r=1,…,n−1 set A_r=(A_{r−1}+t(r))*(1+δ(r)); return A_{n−1}. The implementation folds in increasing index order with an initially absent accumulator, then defaults an absent final accumulator to zero.",

      "status": "understood"
    },

      "meaning": "For natural b,m, s,j∈Fin(m), and i∈Fin(b), ι(s,j,i)∈Fin((b*m)*m) has natural value i+b*(j+m*s). It first encodes (s,j), then pairs that code with i, and transports the result along (m*m)*b=(b*m)*m.",

    {

      "For every b,m∈ℕ, under hypotheses 0<b and 0<m.",

      "For every x,y:Fin((b*m)*m)→ℝ and every error record e∈E(b,m). These choices are universally quantified; no independence or probabilistic assumptions are imposed.",

      "|T(x,y,e)−∑_{k=0}^{N−1}x(k)y(k)| ≤ γ(u,K)*∑_{k=0}^{N−1}|x(k)y(k)|, where N=(b*m)*m, K=b+2*(m−1), and γ(u,K)=K*u/(1−K*u), with K interpreted as a real in the quotient."

    "hypotheses": [
      "b and m are strictly positive natural numbers.",
      "u is a nonnegative real number.",
      "Every product error satisfies |p(k)|≤u for k∈Fin(N).",
      "Every within-block addition error satisfies |a(s,j,i)|≤u for s,j∈Fin(m), i∈Fin(b).",

    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin(n)={0,…,n−1}. Set N=(b*m)*m and K=b+2*(m−1). Natural subtraction is truncated; because m>0, m−1 is the usual predecessor.",
      "An error record E(b,m) is a tuple (p,a,c,d) with p:Fin(N)→ℝ, a:Fin(m)→Fin(m)→Fin(b)→ℝ, c:Fin(m)→Fin(m)→ℝ, and d:Fin(m)→ℝ. Valid(e,u) is the conjunction of all four componentwise absolute-value bounds.",

    "proposition_plain_english": "For every pair of positive natural numbers b,m, every nonnegative real u, every two real arrays x,y of length N=b*m*m, and every collection of product and addition perturbations bounded in absolute value by u, consider the specified three-level computation: perturb each coordinate product, sequentially sum b products per block, sequentially sum m blocks per outer group, and sequentially sum the m outer groups. Each sequential sum copies its first term and perturbs each subsequent addition by a factor 1+δ. If K*u<1 for K=b+2*(m−1), the absolute difference between this computed scalar and the exact dot product is at most [K*u/(1−K*u)] times the sum of the absolute coordinate products."

      "Fin(n)={0,…,n−1}. Set N=(b*m)*m and K=b+2*(m−1). Natural subtraction is truncated; because m>0, m−1 is the usual predecessor.",

      "Define C(s)=S_m(j↦B(s,j), j↦c(s,j)) and T(x,y,e)=S_m(s↦C(s), s↦d(s)).",

      "All operations in these definitions are real operations. Perturbed multiplication is explicitly xy*(1+p); perturbed addition is explicitly (a+t)*(1+δ). The initial assignment at each summation level has no addition perturbation.",
      "The error measure is scalar absolute value. Its scale factor is ∑|x(k)y(k)|, the sum of absolute coordinate products, rather than |∑x(k)y(k)|."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every pair of positive natural numbers b,m, every nonnegative real u, every two real arrays x,y of length N=b*m*m, and every collection of product and addition perturbations bounded in absolute value by u, consider the specified three-level computation: perturb each coordinate product, sequentially sum b products per block, sequentially sum m blocks per outer group, and sequentially sum the m outer groups. Each sequential sum copies its first term and perturbs each subsequent addition by a factor 1+δ. If K*u<1 for K=b+2*(m−1), the absolute difference between this computed scalar and the exact dot product is at most [K*u/(1−K*u)] times the sum of the absolute coordinate products."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "The conclusion is conditional: for choices failing positivity, nonnegativity, validity, or K*u<1, the implication makes no error-bound assertion.",
    "There is no empty-domain vacuity under the hypotheses: b,m>0 imply N>0 and nonempty index sets at every summation level.",
    "The assumptions are jointly satisfiable for every positive b,m: choose u=0 and all error entries zero. More generally, K≥1 and the allowed range is 0≤u<1/K.",
    "The entries a(s,j,0), c(s,0), and d(0) are bounded by validity but never used. If b=1 or m=1, the corresponding summation levels perform no additions; the model and bound still apply.",
    "If every coordinate product is zero, the right side is zero and the model output is also zero. Likewise, u=0 forces all errors to zero and yields exact agreement; these are substantive special cases, not contradictory hypotheses.",
    "Although γ is defined even at a zero denominator through totalized real division, that case is excluded by K*u<1."
  ]
}
